cells.tense: You are holding something people before you thought worth keeping, and right now you are handing it on in words that shift with whoever receives them.
cells.act: add a little or take a little away, and sense the difference
cells.ask: Take one piece of what you carry forward — a phrase, a step, a way of doing it — and add or drop a little. Stop there and feel what shifted before you keep it or turn it back.
cells.core:
You inherit things, and you let them change while they are with you. A tradition stays alive only if it can be said in the next voice, and yours is a next voice. You pass things on by adapting — belonging without having to match a template. The shape underneath is what holds; the surface is meant to move.

What the adjustment asks of you is small. Choose a phrase you repeat, or a way you do a thing, and shift it a little in one direction. One dial. Then pause and sense what is different before you decide. No plan past that, no announcement. What you notice in that turn is what keeps what you pass on breathing instead of going hard.
cells.sheetLine: You keep what matters by letting it speak in your own voice.
cells.verb: Receive what has been passed down and hand it on in words that make it live.
cells.place: The bare shape of a thing seen apart from any single example.

cells.tense: You are holding a pattern so tightly that nobody can get through it, braced against a version of the world that has not arrived and will not be written the way you need it to be.
cells.act: stop holding up the false thing and watch it come down
cells.ask: Find a structure you keep propping up — a rule, a version, a way things have to be — and take your hand off it. Watch what happens as it comes down, and stay with it a while.
cells.core:
Something you carry has hardened into a form that lets no one through, including you. The window got sealed because a draft came in, and now the shape sits there perfect and shut. It reads as loyalty. From the other side it feels like a locked door. The meaning was not the seal. The meaning was the thing moving through.

Stop holding up the piece that needs to fall. Not the whole thing — one piece. Find the structure you keep pushing back into place, and take your hand off it. Let it come down and look at what is underneath. A false thing falling is a clearing, not a catastrophe. What is true in what you carry survives it.

cells.tense: You are at a door that already closed behind you, and the tradition you came from went quiet — every generation building again what you never got handed.
cells.act: step back far enough to see the whole arrangement
cells.ask: Choose something that keeps happening and step back from this round of it until you can see the whole arrangement — who is where, what moves what. Keep the distance a few minutes, then let it be.
cells.core:
You do not have a shared frame to stand in, so you build one each time, alone. That is not a failure of yours; it is the bare shelf. The mind is sharp and there is nothing on it. Nothing got passed down because nothing came through the door you are still beside.

What helps a seat running low is distance. Something keeps happening — at work, with people, in yourself — and you are close to it, inside this round of it. Step back until the whole arrangement is visible: who is where, what moves what. Not why this time, not what it means about you. Just the arrangement. Hold that view a few minutes and change nothing in it. Seeing how a thing works is not the tradition, but it is a way back toward one: shape first, then people, then something worth handing on.

cells.tense: You are already writing in a room you don't think is yours — people took something from how you said it, and you are calling it just talking.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: Look back over one conversation where you explained something and it landed. Find the single move you made — the example, the turn of phrase — and mark it as yours. Nothing more.
cells.core:
You are already passing something on, and the pen is down without your name on it. You show people a shape under their problem — you say it plain, you say it once — and something in them opens. You would call it a conversation. They would call it the thing that made it clear.

The hand is yours. The correction is small: take one conversation where you explained something and it landed, and find the single move you made — a comparison, a turn of phrase, a question. Mark that move as yours. Don't announce it afterward. No lurch into a role. That one correction to how you are counting what you already do puts the author quietly beside their own work.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the teacher. You just don't see it.

attempts.check: The one claim the record does not support: that the person is already teaching or transmitting before they know it — the Unacknowledged kernel names the mechanism, but whether it lands on them as theirs is not established. The reader could reasonably say the reading is over-general about a life it cannot see, especially where the Too Much and Too Little cells locate a condition rather than describe it. The ask survives being wrong: none of the four acts depends on the diagnosis being right, and each is doable without the person being anyone in particular. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'You're already the teacher' — I'm writing it once, plain, and letting the person keep their own name for it.
